body:
Scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities today across the 81 live contracts pulled from Kalshi and Polymarket. That's the normal state of affairs — most scans find nothing, and today is no exception rather than a gap in coverage.

The contract ladders on both venues are broadly consistent with where gold actually sits right now. Gold rose to $4,350.36 on September 11, 2026, up 0.76% from the previous day, and other trackers put it in a similar band: gold trading near $4,366 to $4,405 depending on feed, as of the morning of September 10, 2026. That lines up with what the order books imply — Kalshi's Above $4,330.99 settle contract for September 30, 2026 is priced near 54-55 cents, roughly a coin-flip, exactly where you'd expect a strike sitting close to spot to trade. Similarly, Polymarket's touch $4,300 contracts for September are priced high (80-84 cents) because spot has already been well above that level most of the month, while touch $3,800 sits near 2-4 cents since a drop of that size would be unusual from here.

The bigger driver of gold's level lately isn't anything in the order books themselves but the macro calendar: US PPI rose 0.4% in August, with annual producer inflation accelerating to 5.4%, above forecast, and investors priced in a more than 70% probability of a Federal Reserve rate move around September 16. That's why the Kalshi and Polymarket ladders show fairly smooth, gradually declining probabilities as strikes rise rather than any kinked mispricing — the market is pricing genuine uncertainty around a live Fed decision, not a stale or thin book. One caveat for readers comparing the two platforms: Kalshi's contracts settle on a specific spot fixing at contract expiry, while Polymarket's touch contracts pay out if price crosses a level at any point during the window — different resolution rules that alone can explain why comparable strikes don't line up perfectly, with no execution edge implied.
headline: No arbitrage found across 81 gold contracts as Kalshi and Polymarket track spot closely
